entities.title: The --json report
entities.summary: One pretty-printed JSON object on stdout for the whole run, which the skill tells agents to parse.
entities.definition: Top-level keys: healthy (bool); checks [{name, state, detail}] with state one of HEALTHY, FAILED, NONE, UNKNOWN, NOT TESTED, UNSUPPORTED; findings [{code, summary, remedy}] with remedy {kind: fix, steps: [names]} or {kind: manual|reboot, text}; wifi_reset_required (bool); plan [{step, blocked_by}]; actions [{step, ok, message}]; facts {macos, interface, service, ipv4, ipv6_global, gateway, default_route_if, public_route_if, tunnels, vpns [{name, state, interface}], split_dns [{domain, nameservers, interface, reachable}], wake_age_secs, over_ssh}; log and state_dir (paths).
guarantees: The key names and the state labels are the ones above.
A finding's code is a fixed string per kind of problem (for example vpn-stale, corp-dns-server, proxy-down).
entities.compatibility: Nothing in the code or README promises stability or versions the format; the step names in steps, plan and actions are display names (Step::name) and change with them.

entities.title: Exit statuses
entities.summary: 0 healthy, 1 problems remain, 2 not macOS, as the --help text and the README say.
consumers: Scripts and agents that run diagnose or fix
guarantees: 0 only when no dimension is FAILED in the final report.
1 when a dimension is FAILED, and also when the state directory cannot be created.
2 when the OS is not macOS.

entities.title: The run's state directory
entities.summary: <state root>/<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>/ holds diagnostic.log, original.json and, after a Wi-Fi cycle, recover.sh.
consumers: The person or agent reading the log or the original settings after a run
entities.definition: original.json is an object of the raw, redacted output of the commands run before any change, keyed getinfo, dns, search, web_proxy, secure_proxy, pac, ifconfig and wifi_power (when a network service is in use), and routes, scutil_dns, scutil_proxy and vpn_list, plus facts (the same summary as the JSON report's facts). recover.sh is a /bin/sh script that sleeps, turns Wi-Fi on for the device and appends a line to diagnostic.log.
guarantees: The directory is private to the user (mode 0700); recover.sh is mode 0700.
Secret-looking lines are dropped from diagnostic.log and from each command's output in original.json.
